evidence: Prime Minister chairs CISR; law gives committee authority to decide cross-government road safety measures, equipment priorities and public information. Article 1 of Decree 75-360; 2023 government meeting.
qualification: Statutory leadership/decision-making, not a 2026 minister-by-minister attendance record

evidence: 1975 decree explicitly includes economy/finance and budget ministerial offices. 2026 Senate report separately describes cross-ministry road-safety expenditure; does not prove CISR approved a fully costed 2023 programme.
qualification: Statutory finance representation; budget is government-system context

evidence: Interior minister is a statutory CISR member; Police and Gendarmerie implement the 2023 drug-driving, speeding and overseas enforcement decisions.
qualification: Formal interior portfolio; operational delivery belongs to law enforcement

evidence: Minister of Justice is a statutory CISR member. 2023 measures 10, 23–29 involve road offences, sanctions, prosecution and victims; 2025 law implements important reforms.
qualification: Formal justice portfolio, not court membership

evidence: No separate fire/rescue authority participation or specific CISR-linked emergency extrication coordination identified in the reviewed 2023 decision package.
qualification: Interior ministry seat is not itself fire-service representation

evidence: Decree lists the minister for Industry, providing a formal industrial portfolio, but no manufacturer/automotive trade group appears as a CISR statutory seat.
qualification: Historical statutory industry portfolio, not automotive manufacturers

evidence: Road-engineering expertise and guidance appear through transport/DSR technical interfaces; 2023 measures 16–17 address road design interventions, but no stand-alone civil-engineering seat confirmed.
Minister for Transport is formally included; CISR determines directions of equipment programmes. Technical implementation on roads is handled by network owners and territorial services.
qualification: Formal transport/road authority portfolio, not each road owner as member

evidence: Minister for Transport is a formal member; 2023 measure 21 involves public/private employers and work-related travel. Transport operator association is not a CISR statutory seat.
qualification: Formal transport ministry seat rather than direct commercial operator representation

evidence: Road Safety Delegation operates driver licensing systems, automated enforcement and crash-statistics interfaces; CISR measures 30–34 cover digital administrative systems. The 1975 text refers to a historical PTT ministry, not proof of a present 2026 digital-ministry seat.
qualification: Administrative digital-delivery interface, not current standing digital minister

evidence: The current legal CISR list and reviewed 2023 decisions do not independently verify a dedicated environmental authority participating in CISR road-safety decisions.
qualification: Climate/energy policy is not inferred from transport membership

evidence: The minister for Urban Planning and Housing is listed in the governing decree; 2023 measure 14 specifically addresses streets with inadequate sidewalks. The ministerial title is historical.
qualification: Statutory housing/planning portfolio, not local planning department attendance

evidence: Health minister is statutorily represented. The 2023 package sets health/fitness and victim-care measures, including annual investments in medical and rehabilitation equipment.
qualification: Formal health portfolio; care remains delivered by health institutions

evidence: CISR 2023 measures 20 and 36 propose local association grants and local overseas partnerships. These are public/stakeholder implementation relationships, not permanent nonprofit seats on CISR.
qualification: Partner link only; CNSR advisory membership must not be counted

evidence: Education minister is a statutory member; 2023 measures 1–2 specify school-based bicycle safety and road-code education.
qualification: Formal education portfolio; national curriculum delivery needs separate tracking

evidence: The decree formally refers to the national solidarity ministerial portfolio; 2023 measures 8 and 9 address victim support and care. The 1975 title is historical and not a verified 2026 department designation.
qualification: Statutory social solidarity portfolio, not confirmed nationwide victim-benefit delivery

evidence: A defence ministerial seat exists in the decree, but no commission-specific civil-defence, evacuation or mass-casualty coordination assignment was confirmed.
qualification: Defence minister is not equivalent to documented civil defence function
